notes.text:
# Oriole desktop client

## Current setting
As of 2025-02-03, the telemetry endpoint listens on loopback port 4318.
The older loopback port 4418 was used from 2024-08-10 through 2025-02-02 and is retired.
The profile identifier is desktop-lilac.
Do not confuse it with the test fixture desktop-lillac, which has an extra l.
The upload interval is fifteen minutes.

## Appearance
The desktop theme is soft charcoal.
The mobile theme has not been selected. The decision log intentionally leaves it open.

## Ownership
The fictional team name is Oriole Tools.
No production hosts are named in this note.

# Oriole ingest workers

## Worker pebble-2

### Current setting
Worker pebble-2 uses write-through cache mode as of 2025-03-11.
Its queue label is q-linen-8.

## Worker pebble-02

### Current setting
Worker pebble-02 uses a read-only mirror cache.
Its queue label is q-linen-80.

## Caution
The names pebble-2 and pebble-02 identify different fictional workers.
A setting from one must not be copied to the other by name similarity.

# Skylark backup agent

## Job identity
The household document job is BKP-HOME-07.
The scratch-media job is BKP-HOME-70.
These identifiers are deliberately similar but not interchangeable.

## Completion sequence
After each copy, verify the generated manifest against the copied objects. Only after that verification passes may stale snapshots be pruned.
A copy that lacks a verified manifest remains incomplete.
Record only the success stamp, never a secret or recovery phrase.

## Timing
BKP-HOME-07 starts on Tuesdays at 02:20 fictional local time.

# Kitchen preferences

## Drinks
After 19:00, the shared tea choice is rooibos rather than black tea.
Morning coffee is medium roast.
Oat drink is kept for guests who request it.

## Cleaning supplies
No dishwasher-tablet brand is recorded; choose any unscented tablet until a brand decision is documented.
Hand soap should be fragrance-free when practical.

## Storage
Everyday mugs belong on the lower oak shelf.
The shelf called lower oke in the old sketch was a spelling error, not a second shelf.

# Laundry and rooms

## Laundry
Use scent-free liquid detergent for all shared laundry. Scented detergent is not approved for shared loads.
Wash kitchen cloths separately from guest towels.
The cold cycle is the default for ordinary clothing.

## Alder room

### Current setting
Keep the reading lamp at the left side of the desk.
Place guest towels in the basket marked GUEST-SAND.

## Aspen room

### Current setting
Keep the reading lamp on the wall shelf.
Place spare blankets in the chest marked GUEST-SAGE.

# Fictional household bookkeeping conventions

## Reimbursements
Record a reimbursement on its approval date, not on the date the receipt was photographed.
If approval is reversed, use the reversal date for the reversing entry.
Project ORC-17 means shared supplies.
Project ORC-71 means learning materials.

## Tax estimates
Round each tax line to the nearest cent before summing the lines. Do not round only the final total.
A half cent rounds away from zero in this notebook.

## Transfers
Transfers between envelopes are not household income.
The memo should name both envelope labels.

# Reimbursement policy notes

## Travel
Transit fares require a trip purpose.
Mileage may be reimbursed when a fictional trip log is complete.
The mileage rate is deliberately not recorded here because it must come from the annual rate table.
No annual rate table is included in these notes.

## Meals
A meal entry lists attendees by role, not by full legal name.
Tips are included in the meal total.

## Review
Reviewer code FINCH-4 is current.
Reviewer code FINCH-04 belonged to the retired sample workflow.

# Decision record: archive bundle format

## Current decision
Decision recorded 2025-01-15: all new archive bundles use tar.zst.
The choice applies to bundles created on or after 2025-01-20.

## Historical context
Zip was the selected format from 2023-06-01 through 2025-01-19. It is not the current choice for new bundles.
Existing zip bundles do not need conversion.

## Deferred item
The filename timestamp style was not decided in this record.

# Decision record: household notifications

## Decision
On 2025-04-06, the household adopted quiet delivery after 21:30. Notifications after that time may show a badge but must not play a sound.
Emergency calls are outside this software notification rule.

## Earlier trial
During March 2025, the trial cutoff was 22:00.
The trial ended when the 21:30 decision took effect.

## Scope
This rule covers the fictional pantry and chore applications.

# Meal constraints

## Mina Vale
Mina has a sesame allergy. Tahini and sesame oil must be excluded from her meals.
Mina is comfortable with oats labeled gluten-free.
Coconut is acceptable for Mina.

## Mena Vail
Mena Vail is a separate fictional guest.
Mena avoids raw tomato by preference.
No allergy information is recorded for Mena.

## Shared meals
Ingredient cards stay beside each serving dish.
A preference must never be silently upgraded to an allergy.

# Fictional guest cards

## Tomas Reed
Tomas can eat gluten but avoids fennel.
He prefers still water with lunch.

## Noor Pell
Noor avoids kiwi fruit.
No caffeine preference or limit was supplied for Noor.
Ask Noor directly before planning a coffee tasting.

## Nori Pell
Nori Pell is a different fictional guest.
Nori prefers decaffeinated coffee after lunch.
The similar names are not a reason to merge their cards.

# Backup retention runbook

## Home documents
Keep daily snapshots for 14 days.
Keep weekly snapshots for 8 weeks.
Keep monthly snapshots for 13 months.
The monthly snapshot is the final verified snapshot of the calendar month.

## Creative drafts
Keep daily snapshots for 30 days.
Keep monthly snapshots for 6 months.

## Restore drill
Run a sample restore on the first Saturday of each month.
A restore drill is successful only when three sampled files open correctly.
Never place credentials in the drill report.

# Synthetic house manual

This manual covers routine fictional household operations.
It contains no addresses, account numbers, or real services.
Each instruction is intentionally written as a complete short line.
Similar labels remain distinct throughout the manual.

## Entry routine

Place ordinary shoes on the slate mat.
Place wet boots on the ribbed tray.
Hang cloth shopping bags on hook BAG-CREAM.
Hook BAG-CREME belongs to the costume box.
Return borrowed umbrellas to the blue stand.
Leave the narrow shelf clear for outgoing parcels.
Check parcel labels before moving any package.
Do not infer a recipient from package color.
Wipe rainwater before storing the floor brush.
Record damaged shared items in the paper log.

## Alder room

### Current setting

The desk faces the blank interior wall.
The left drawer holds plain stationery.
The right drawer holds drawing supplies.
The low basket is labeled ALDER-GUEST.
The lamp timer ends at 22:10.
The radiator dial normally stays at two.
The striped cushion belongs on the wooden chair.
The solid cushion belongs on the window bench.
Keep the ventilation gap unobstructed.
Do not store books against the radiator.

## Aspen room

### Current setting

The desk faces the courtyard window.
The left drawer holds drawing supplies.
The right drawer holds plain stationery.
The low basket is labeled ASPEN-GUEST.
The lamp timer ends at 21:50.
The radiator dial normally stays at one.
The striped cushion belongs on the window bench.
The solid cushion belongs on the wooden chair.
Keep the curtain clear of the heater.
Do not move Alder labels into Aspen.

## Kitchen opening

Open the small blind before breakfast.
Fill the drinking jug with fresh water.
Set the compost crock beside the cutting board.
Check that yesterday's cloth is in the wash basket.
Put clean cloths in the drawer marked CLOTH-3.
Drawer CLOTH-03 holds table mats instead.
Keep wooden tools away from the soaking basin.
Allow the kettle exterior to dry before wiping it.
Use the oldest dated oat drink first.
Move no unlabeled jar into shared storage.

## Kitchen closing

Empty the compost crock after the evening meal.
Wipe the work surface with an unscented cleaner.
Leave the steel pan dry on its hook.
Place the cast pan on the lower rack.
Check that the refrigerator door is fully closed.
Write low staples on the chalk list.
Date opened grains with the calendar date.
Store sharp tools in the fitted drawer.
Leave one clean towel by the sink.
Turn off the window light last.

## Pantry labels

Label PAN-OAT identifies ordinary rolled oats.
Label PAN-OATS identifies the sealed guest container.
Label PAN-RICE identifies long-grain rice.
Label PAN-RICES is not in use.
Use clear month names on pantry dates.
Never identify allergens by lid color alone.
Keep sesame ingredients in the marked closed bin.
Keep guest-safe utensils in their own sleeve.
Replace any label that cannot be read.
Do not reuse an allergen label for another item.

## Freezer routine

List frozen meals on card FREEZE-A.
List frozen ingredients on card FREEZE-B.
Cross out an item when it leaves the freezer.
Add the prepared date beside every meal.
Use the upper basket for vegetables.
Use the middle basket for prepared meals.
Use the lower basket for bread and pastry.
Keep loose ice out of labeled food baskets.
Defrost only during a planned inventory day.
The appliance make and model are not documented here.

## Laundry sorting

Place white kitchen cloths in bin WASH-K1.
Place colored kitchen cloths in bin WASH-K2.
Place guest towels in bin WASH-G1.
Place cleaning rags in bin WASH-R1.
Do not combine cleaning rags with guest towels.
Use cold water for routine clothing.
Use the care label when it requires another cycle.
Air-dry wool items on the mesh frame.
Return empty baskets to the upper shelf.
Log a leaking container before replacing it.

## Household purchasing

Use list HOME-WEEK for routine groceries.
Use list HOME-LONG for durable replacements.
A listed item is not automatically approved.
Mark substitutions beside the original item.
Keep fictional warranty slips in folder PAPER-6.
Folder PAPER-06 contains craft templates.
Compare unit prices using the same unit.
Record a return when the shop accepts it.
Do not count store credit as cash received.
Avoid recording payment credentials in this manual.

## Envelope bookkeeping

Envelope FOOD covers shared groceries.
Envelope HOME covers routine household supplies.
Envelope GUEST covers agreed guest preparations.
Envelope LEARN covers books and classes.
Move money between envelopes as a transfer.
Do not classify an envelope transfer as income.
Date a correction on the day it is entered.
Preserve the original memo in a correction note.
Round only according to the relevant convention note.
Leave uncertain categories for review.

## Receipt handling

Photograph a receipt while all edges are visible.
Keep the original until the monthly check finishes.
Name a receipt image with its purchase date.
Add the approval date in the bookkeeping record.
Do not invent a project code from a similar label.
Use ORC-17 only for shared supplies.
Use ORC-71 only for learning materials.
Flag an unreadable total for manual review.
Record refunds separately from purchases.
Destroy duplicate paper only after verification.

## Software test profiles

Profile LARK-4 simulates a morning schedule.
Profile LARK-04 simulates an evening schedule.
Profile WREN-A uses a pale interface.
Profile WREN-B uses a dark interface.
Test profiles contain synthetic content only.
Never copy a test token into another profile.
Reset test queues after a completed scenario.
Keep scenario names shorter than forty characters.
Date accepted scenarios in the change note.
Leave undecided appearance choices unset.

## Software change notes

State the previous value before the new value.
Give the effective date for a changed default.
Call a temporary setting a trial.
Call a ratified setting a decision.
Do not describe a retired value as current.
Preserve exact hyphens in identifiers.
Preserve meaningful leading zeroes in identifiers.
Explain similar names when confusion is plausible.
Keep secrets outside ordinary change notes.
Review examples for fictional data before saving.

## Backup preparation

Close files that are still being edited.
Confirm that the source label matches the job.
Confirm that the destination has enough space.
Start only the intended fictional job identifier.
Wait for the copy stage to report completion.
Generate a manifest for the completed copy.
Compare the manifest with copied objects.
Mark the run verified only after comparison.
Prune nothing from an unverified run.
Write the completion date in the run log.

## Restore practice

Choose sample files from different folders.
Restore samples into the isolated practice area.
Open each restored sample with its normal reader.
Compare the sample against its manifest entry.
Record whether each sample opened correctly.
Remove practice copies after the review.
Keep the original backup untouched.
Escalate any mismatch before routine pruning.
Do not include credentials in the report.
Use synthetic examples in training notes.

## Meal planning

Read every current guest card before planning.
Separate allergies from stated preferences.
Keep ingredient packaging until service ends.
Place an ingredient card beside every dish.
Use a clean utensil for each serving dish.
Ask when a restriction is unrecorded.
Never infer one guest's answer from another's.
Treat similar guest names as distinct identities.
Offer plain water without requiring a preference.
Document a change only after the guest confirms it.

## Quiet hours

Dim shared-room lights at 21:15.
Use headphones for spoken audio after 21:30.
Allow software badges during quiet delivery.
Disable ordinary software sounds after 21:30.
Keep emergency calling rules separate.
Close soft-latch doors without forcing them.
Prepare morning items before quiet hours.
Keep hallway conversations brief at night.
Move noisy chores to the daytime list.
Review temporary exceptions the next morning.

## Monthly review

Check pantry labels for legibility.
Check household lists for stale entries.
Check envelope transfers for clear memos.
Check reimbursement approvals for dates.
Check backup logs for verified manifests.
Check restore drills for readable samples.
Check guest cards for confirmed updates.
Check software notes for effective dates.
Archive completed paper checklists together.
Leave unresolved questions explicitly open.

## Manual boundaries

This manual does not contain any password.
This manual does not name a real network.
This manual does not provide banking coordinates.
This manual does not identify a real person.
An omitted fact must not be guessed.
An undecided fact must remain undecided.
A historical setting must remain historical.
A current decision must include its scope.
A similar name is not equivalent evidence.
The final review should preserve these boundaries.
